description: Synthetic 100-day cycle where stable categories (labour and machinery) drift 8% above expected-to-date. In tiered mode this is correctly classified as normal (within the 10% stable allowance), whereas a flat 7% rule raises a false alarm and proposal baseline (variance > 0) flags as alert.

expenses.notes: Weeding labour with 8% seasonal wage fluctuation

expectedAlertEvents.derivation: Hand calculation: Day 50 linear phase is 0.50. expectedToDate = 100,000 * 0.50 = 50,000. actual = 54,000. variancePct = (54,000 - 50,000) / 50,000 = +4,000 / 50,000 = +0.0800 (+8.00%). Tiered rule (stable category): Normal allowance is <= 10.0%. Since 8.00% <= 10.0%, tier is normal. Proposal baseline (v > 0): triggers alert (false positive). A hypothetical flat 7% rule would trigger an unwanted false alarm.
